Recorded claim:
The first LineReader async landing for Bug 1893307 caused permanent NNTP test failures and was backed out. Bugzilla and D210555 attribute this to an exposed promise-chain rejection and a null runningUri during NNTP completion. The reland added optional chaining before SetUrlState and passed a full Try run. The reviewer asked for an automated long-response test, then accepted with the stated I/O testing limit. This illustrates that a shared parser timing change needs POP3 and NNTP test coverage and careful review of completion callbacks; a green local POP3 observation alone did not cover the change.

Provenance: 939fbe1a6d1d9cc3f8e1bf15f528b733b033dccdf077f7dc24fb8a12e37690c4. Original evidence IDs: 439682bbb0e339839633c1cc6329271014583addd7e727ce4ade5530e6a5aa21, 5fd663419d754cd71c11c8e2b44eb4c2714864234ca69ab460baf4aeed8b5042, d1fcb3164c0fc1850da296b553dba66a2659a4da0b3510004af6d5c0d4fcd951.
This is a recorded historical interpretation, not independent source verification. Source quotes from personal imports or unconfirmed-access records remain private. Historical test results are reported outcomes; no tests were rerun for this backfill.

title: Recorded lesson: Check shared protocol callers when an async change exposes old callback failures
